Definition: properly, something set apart, i.e. (abstractly) dedication (of a priet or Nazirite); hence (concretely) unshorn locks; also (by implication) a chaplet (especially of royalty)
BiblicalUsage: The crown of separation is worn on the forehead and lived in the body. The high priest wears the golden plate, the holy crown, on his mitre; the Nazirite keeps the days of his separation from everything of the vine; and the crown taken from Saul's head is carried to David as the sign that the king is dead.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe separation is a crown, not a chain: the priest wears it, the Nazirite lives it, and the king loses it when he falls. The priest's crown is gold on the forehead, and the Nazirite's crown is a life kept apart — both of them are worn in public.
